pulls.title: net: limit relative ban times to uint32
pulls.body:
`BanMan::Ban` computes the ban end as `GetTime() + bantime` (banman.cpp:140). `setban` and `-bantime` both accept any int64, so a relative bantime close to `INT64_MAX`:

```
setban 1.2.3.5 add 9223372036854775807
```

returns success, but the sum overflows. UBSan reports:

```
src/banman.cpp:140:73: runtime error: signed integer overflow: 1790412558 + 9223372036854775807 cannot be represented in type 'int64_t'
```

Without UBSan the result wraps negative, the ban is treated as already expired, and it is silently dropped. With `-bantime=9223372036854775807` the same happens to every `setban add` that uses the default duration.

This limits relative ban times to uint32 (about 136 years):

- `setban` rejects a relative bantime above `UINT32_MAX` with "Error: bantime is too large"
- `-bantime` is parsed as `uint32_t`, so larger values saturate at `UINT32_MAX`

Absolute timestamps are unchanged.

The added cases in `rpc_setban.py` check that `UINT32_MAX + 1` and `INT64_MAX` are rejected, that `UINT32_MAX` is accepted, and that with `-bantime=INT64_MAX` a default-duration ban is listed with a duration of `UINT32_MAX`. Both parts fail on master and pass with the change. `p2p_disconnect_ban.py` still passes.

AI tools were used to help find this issue and to prepare the patch and test.

pulls.title: wallet: reject recipient amounts above MAX_MONEY
pulls.body:
`CreateTransaction` checks that recipient amounts aren't negative, but not that they're within `MAX_MONEY`. `CreateTransactionInternal` then sums them into `recipients_sum` (spend.cpp:1100) with no range check, and that sum can overflow.

Easiest way to hit it is `fundrawtransaction` with a raw tx that has two outputs of 2^62 sat. It can also be reached with only valid amounts through `walletcreatefundedpsbt`/`send`/`sendmany` and a few thousand 21M BTC outputs. The "Transaction too large" check only runs after coin selection, so it doesn't stop this. On master the node aborts:

```
Assertion failed: (!m_selected_inputs.empty()), function RecalculateWaste, file coinselection.cpp, line 904.
```

UBSan reports the overflow at spend.cpp:1100 first. With other values the sum wraps to a small positive number instead, and `fundrawtransaction` returns success for a tx with outputs of 46116860184 BTC each.

This checks every amount and the running sum against `MoneyRange` in the existing recipients loop of `CreateTransactionInternal`, before the amount is added to `recipients_sum`, and returns "Transaction output amount must be valid" before coin selection starts. The same check rejects negative amounts, so the separate negative check in `CreateTransaction` is removed. The new `test_outputs_above_max_money` in `wallet_fundrawtransaction.py` covers a single output above MAX_MONEY, two outputs whose sum is above it, a sum that overflows int64, and a negative output. On master the first case returns "Insufficient funds" and the overflow case crashes the node; with the fix all of them get the new error. `wallet_fundrawtransaction.py`, `wallet_send.py`, `wallet_basic.py` and `rpc_psbt.py` pass.

pulls.title: streams: avoid termination on buffered write failure
pulls.body:
**Problem:** Block and undo writers buffer serialized data, then rely on the `BufferedWriter` destructor to write the remaining bytes.
`fwrite()` can report fewer bytes written than requested after a local storage error, e.g., if the filesystem fills up while a block is being written (my 1 TB benchmarking servers have recently been filling up, so I've been seeing these failures more often).
`AutoFile::write_buffer()` converts that result into an exception, and because the destructor is implicitly non-throwing, the exception invokes `std::terminate` instead of reaching normal storage-error handling.
Calling `flush()` before destruction is insufficient on its own because a failed flush leaves the same bytes pending, so the destructor retries the write while the original exception unwinds.

I introduced this bug in #31551 when adding the `BufferedWriter`.

**Fix:** `BufferedWriter` now clears the pending byte count before writing, preventing a destructor retry after a failed explicit flush.
Block and undo writers flush before destruction, so write failures follow normal storage-error handling instead of terminating the process.

<details>
<summary>Manual short-write reproducer</summary>

```sh
sed -i '' '122s/src.size()/0/' src/streams.cpp
cmake -B build && cmake --build build -j && build/bin/bitcoind -regtest -datadir="$(mktemp -d)"; echo "exit=$?"
```

With implicit flushing, `bitcoind` aborts:

> libc++abi: terminating due to uncaught exception of type std::__1::ios_base::failure: AutoFile::write_buffer: write failed: unspecified iostream_category error
> zsh: abort      build/bin/bitcoind -regtest -datadir="$(mktemp -d)"
> exit=134

With explicit flushing, it reports `Failed to write genesis block` and exits 1 instead of terminating the process:

> Shutdown done
> exit=1
</details>

pulls.title: depends: keep local source archives in WORK_PATH
pulls.body:
Local package tarballs are generated from the current checkout, but depends caches them alongside downloaded archives in `SOURCES_PATH`. When checkouts share that directory, a cached local tarball can be newer than another checkout's source files, causing depends to build the wrong sources with a valid checksum and build ID.

Store local package tarballs and their checksum stamps in `WORK_PATH/local-sources` instead. `WORK_PATH` is per-checkout by default, so generated snapshots stay with their checkout while downloaded sources remain shareable through `SOURCES_PATH`. Existing mtime-based invalidation is unchanged.

This also handles `contrib/guix/guix-build`, which mounts each checkout at `/bitcoin`. Distinguishing local tarballs by absolute source path cannot isolate those builds when `SOURCES_PATH` is shared.

Validation: focused checks reproduced the same-path collision with the path-hash approach and verified isolation with this change. Host/container source checksums and build IDs match; archive reuse, refresh after an edit, and downloaded-source paths were also checked. No full Guix build was run.

Addresses #35764.

pulls.title: test: Check bitcoin wrapper child exit status on windows
pulls.body:
Follow-up to #36105, which makes the Windows `bitcoin.exe` wrapper wait for its child and forward the child's exit code. This adds the functional test for that.

The case worth covering is exit code -1. The first version of the wrapper used `_spawnvp(_P_WAIT)`, which returns -1 both when the spawn fails and when the child started fine and exited with -1, so `bitcoin.exe` reported a startup error and exited 1 instead of passing -1 through. #36105 now uses `_P_NOWAIT` + `_cwait`, which keeps the spawn result and the child status separate. Against the old launcher this test fails at `not(1 == 4294967295)`.

The test copies `bitcoin.exe` into a temp dir next to a copy of `cmd.exe` named `bitcoind.exe`, so `bitcoin -M node /d /c exit N` runs the fake child, and checks 0, 1 and -1 come back unchanged. Windows reports exit codes as unsigned 32-bit, so -1 arrives as 4294967295. It also checks the wrapper adds nothing to stdout/stderr. The exit code test is Windows only.

ryanofsky preferred keeping the runtime fix in #36105 and reviewing the test here (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36190#issuecomment-5603692520), so this is the same commit he briefly carried in his branch. The branch still contains #36105's commits and should land after it.

Checked on a native Windows 11 clang/UCRT release build, wallet/GUI/IPC off:

```text
cmake --build build --target bitcoin bitcoind bitcoin-cli
python test/functional/tool_bitcoin.py --configfile=build/test/config.ini --tmpdir=build/tool-bitcoin-exit-status
```

Fails against the pre-fix launcher, passes against the fixed one, and the rest of `tool_bitcoin.py` still passes. Use a fresh `--tmpdir` when re-running.

pulls.body: Only P2SH-P2WPKH inputs are eligible, which require a non-empty witness. pulls.title: init: log resolved datadir path
pulls.body:
Because the data directory may be a symlink, also log the path it resolves to, so `debug.log` files show the actual location for that run.

This patch would mostly help developers. I've been testing a potential performance PR across different data directories (for example, SSD versus HDD). After each run, I save the `debug.log` file. It would be nice if the `debug.log` file showed which data directory was used for that run.

There are two ways to change which data directory to use: `-datadir=` on the command line, or by making the default path a symlink. If a _script_ starts `bitcoind` (e.g., on an RPi with a whole infrastructure, like Umbrel or myNode), changing the startup command arguments may be inconvenient or not even possible. It's easy to change the default directory to be a symlink. But in that case, `debug.log` doesn't show where the actual data directory is located. This patch adds one line to the logging startup output showing the resolved data directory path (after following symlinks).

I don't think a separate test is needed. I haven't tested on all platforms, but this patch uses primitives already used elsewhere, so it should work everywhere.

Here's an example of the additional line this patch logs during startup, just after the `Using data directory` line (omitting the timestamp prefix). I'll show both here for context (only the second line is added):
```
Using data directory /home/larry/.bitcoin
Resolved data directory /sd/.bitcoin
```
The patch could print this line only if the resolved path differs from the `Using data directory` path, but we may as well print it every time, because it's only one extra line, and this way any scripts that look for the resolved path are simpler (they can depend on it always being there).

torcontrol: send -torpassword hex-encoded to avoid escaping bugs
pulls.body:
The Tor password was sent as a `QuotedString` with only double quotes escaped; as Tor interprets backslash escapes inside it, any password containing a backslash was mangled (or left the string unterminated).

The Tor Control spec deliberately allows the token to be sent as unquoted hex "to avoid escaping issues", as the `SAFECOOKIE` response already is. This patch does the same for the password, and also adds a functional test covering backslashes and quotes.

pulls.title: i2p: pass base32 address directly to stream connect
pulls.body:
As the SAM protocol accepts a `.b32.i2p` address as the `DESTINATION` parameter for the `STREAM CONNECT` command, the `NAMING LOOKUP` round trip can be skipped on every outbound connection.

This should ostensibly make failure handling more accurate in certain situations as well, since a peer that cannot be resolved now returns `CANT_REACH_PEER`/`TIMEOUT` rather than there being an empty `VALUE=` key in the lookup reply. A missing `VALUE=` is a proxy error, so the attempt isn't recorded in AddrMan.

Router implementation versions that support this (Java I2P 0.9.48, i2pd 2.38.0) are older than ones supporting `i2cp.leaseSetEncType=6,4` (see #35696), so there should be no compatibility issues here.

Source:
https://i2p.net/en/docs/api/samv3/#sam-virtual-streams-connect
